context:
Goal: after a compaction the session's handoff is written for it, so it cannot be skipped or slip away.
Problem (rule): today a hook only nudges the session to write its own handoff, and sessions have skipped it (the batch runner lost its queue this way). You asked at 22:49 CST whether a guard can do the handoff itself, like the judge hooks do. Your own ruling blocks it: decision precompact-handoff, item 4, says "It must work in the desktop app with no other login. No second `claude -p` with its own command-line login. So no mode of `hooks/precompact_handoff.py` calls a model." The ruling is yours, so it needs your word to change.
What protected: the handoff hook works in the desktop app without a second login.
What protects it now: unmeasured. The judge hooks already call a model through the shared helper `invoke_model` in hooks/decision_watch.py, which runs `claude -p`; whether that works on your Mac desktop app, or silently reads "unknown", has not been measured here (the cloud has no guard.log).
Based on (read): the decision text above; the helper's own comment ("Run the judgment prompt through `claude -p`, isolated"; any failure is reported as unknown, never guessed); the consultant's account of your 22:49 CST ask, relayed.
Departs from: main — the post-compaction hook never calls a model; a changes that for one call per compaction, b keeps it.
Meanwhile: nothing changes; the nudge and the audit steps stay as they are.
home: decision precompact-handoff, item 4; step handoff-written-by-hook; hooks/decision_watch.py invoke_model
lastAnswer: Owner 22:52 CST (relayed by the consultant): a subagent writes the handoff at the checkpoints; claude -p is no longer the premise.

options.gain: A handoff always exists after a compaction; the session cannot skip it.
options.label: The post-compaction hook calls the model once per compaction and writes the handoff itself; the session reads it and corrects it (recommended by the consultant)
options.lose: Item 4 of your ruling is replaced. If `claude -p` has no login on a desktop session, the hook cannot write it and must fall back to today's nudge, so the gain is not proven there until a Mac session tests it.

options.gain: Your ruling stands; no model call at compaction.
options.label: Keep the nudge; the audit steps and the inbox check carry the rest
options.lose: A session can still skip the handoff, which is what happened to the batch runner.

reply: Closed on your 22:52 CST words, relayed by the consultant (triage did not see them). Filed as ruling own-810-subagent-writes-handoff. Step handoff-written-by-hook is ready: the hook refuses Stop at each checkpoint and after compaction until the session spawns one Sonnet subagent that rewrites the handoff; the old no-model-call sentence in precompact-handoff is rewritten in place. That mechanism is the consultant's reading of your words, not yours.
short: Let a hook write the handoff after compaction?
title: Should a hook write the post-compaction handoff itself, replacing your ruling that no handoff mode calls a model?
why: Your own ruling (precompact-handoff, item 4) says no handoff mode calls a model; only you can change it.
